determinism.canonicalization: one closed canonical JSON representation exists for every valid term and semantically unordered CRT parts are sorted by canonical child bytes
determinism.identity: full SHA-256 binds the exact canonical term object byte framing and no theorem or authority claim enters that digest
determinism.normalization: integer polynomials trim trailing zeroes and rational coefficients use fractions.Fraction canonical numerator and denominator
determinism.platform: behavior depends only on declared exact bytes and CPython integer, tuple, Fraction, JSON, dataclass, and SHA-256 semantics, never on locale, clock, host, checkout, environment, package discovery, or hash iteration order

effects.mutation: caller bytes and collections are never retained or mutated; successful values own immutable tuples and exact scalar values
effects.solver: none and no producer, checker, CAS, SAT, SMT, transport, plugin, or proof-assistant module is imported or executed

ensures: Successful parsing returns exactly one ResidueTerm, CRTTerm, SumInductionTerm, or PolynomialIdentityTerm whose complete reachable value graph has been revalidated inside fixed budgets.

Every public proof-term class has a closed constructor, frozen slots, final subclass behavior, tuple-owned children and coefficients, stable structural equality and hashing, blocked pickle reduction, and identity-preserving safe copy behavior.

Public residue, crt, sum_induction, and polynomial_identity factories validate before construction, copy caller collections, normalize exact polynomials and fractions, and cannot mint checker or theorem authority.

proof_term_to_bytes emits canonical UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes, no floats, no duplicate keys, and exactly one trailing newline; parse_proof_term accepts only those exact canonical bytes.

term_sha256 is the full lowercase SHA-256 of the exact canonical term object bytes with one trailing newline, excluding the envelope and digest field; stale, truncated, substituted, or ambiguously framed identities fail closed.
CRT children have one canonical bytewise order, polynomial trailing zeroes are removed while retaining one zero coefficient, and Fraction values use a positive coprime denominator.

object.__new__, object.__setattr__, dataclass replacement, subclassing, alias mutation, pickle, malformed JSON, duplicate keys, unknown tags, cycles, over-depth graphs, over-size collections, and oversized integers cannot bypass boundary revalidation.
No proof term exposes verified, theorem, authority, certificate, or checker-attestation state; mathematical checking and theorem issuance remain exclusively assigned to MH-032.

epistemics.invalid: any structural, canonical, identity, type, graph, or budget failure yields no proof term and no authority
epistemics.parsed: the exact canonical bytes represent one structurally valid immutable proof term under this contract
epistemics.structurally_valid: the in-memory graph matches the closed v1 algebra and budgets but makes no mathematical truth claim
epistemics.untrusted: a producer, caller, deserializer, or forged object may supply candidate structure but cannot grant theorem or checker authority
epistemics.verified: not an outcome of this contract; only the independently extracted MH-032 checker may issue checker attestation

invariants: The public algebra is exactly ResidueTerm(modulus, polynomial), CRTTerm(parts), SumInductionTerm(summand, closed_form), and PolynomialIdentityTerm(lhs, rhs), created only by validating factories or canonical parsing.
Proof terms are values, not theorems: construction, equality, hashing, serialization, deserialization, copying, or provenance identity never promotes an epistemic tier.
Every boundary traversal uses exact type checks; bool is never an integer, float never enters exact arithmetic, and no implicit int, Fraction, string, iterable, or JSON coercion is permitted.

Every nonzero integer has bit_length at most 4096, every polynomial has one through 4096 canonical coefficients, every CRT has one through 1024 children, and each graph has at most 4096 nodes and depth at most 64.

Repeated immutable child references are allowed and counted by occurrence, while an active object-identity recurrence is a cycle and fails before hashing, equality, representation, or recursion can escape.

The implementation imports only __future__, dataclasses, fractions, hashlib, json, and typing and stays within the MH-030 dependency-minimal target allowlist with no third-party, dynamic-import, filesystem, process, network, clock, random, environment, or floating-point capability.
The implementation carries exactly one top-level MH-C-PROOF-TERM-001 contract ID and accepted SHA-256 binding, and the declared parse_proof_term signature resolves exactly.
Legacy mathhead.discovery.kernel proof and Theorem types remain non-authoritative migration inputs until MH-032 replaces the checker boundary; this contract does not silently bless or serialize them.
raises: ProofTermValidationError with kind type, encoding, json, duplicate, schema, canonical, identity, term, cycle, or budget for every ordinary invalid input or forged in-memory object.
PermissionError for direct public construction of proof-term classes and TypeError for subclass or pickle attempts.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit never become an ordinary validation result and never produce a proof term.
requires: The accepted MH-C-WORKFLOW-001=99cfdf17371938af65c4203c02cbaac0bf73470e9fab59f7a6d62360fc0b7cca and MH-C-TRUST-BASE-001=2d2c23da4d3b167c5220c7548602f11403af7634031c438a8f61ac8e3e191456 govern this critical trust-boundary type.
Input is an exact bytes value no larger than 1048576 bytes; text, bytearray, memoryview, streams, paths, and implicit coercions are rejected.
The wire envelope is governed by closed Draft 2020-12 schema docs/contracts/schemas/proof-term-v1.schema.json=647bfd65e611a4e427ff36dd9e2c3e07af4839aa7d91a180d55af3e5e5ea99f7.
The only v1 rule tags are residue, crt, sum_induction, and polynomial_identity; every object and rule rejects unknown or missing fields.
Integer coefficients, moduli, rational numerators, and rational denominators are exact Python integers but never booleans, floats, strings, or coercible substitutes.
